item.title: UK Charts: Orbitals Floats Out Of The Top 10 As Last Week's Newbies Hold Down The Podium

description.p: Defying gravity.We are back with our latest look at the UK charts, and after last week's excitement with all those newcomers, it's a slightly more familiar picture this time.The wonderful Switch 2 exclusive, Orbitals (which landed in third place in its debut week, let's not forget), has drifted down to 18th this time, likely having found the majority of its audience right from the jump. The other two previous podium holders, The Blood of the Dawnwalker and Onimusha: Way of the Sword, hold down the top spots once again, but flip positions this time — Switch 2 sales continue to make up a small 7% of the latter.Read the full article on nintendolife.com

item.title: New Trademark Seemingly Reveals The Title For Lies Of P Sequel

description.p: O RLY?A new trademark from developer Neowiz has seemingly revealed the title for its upcoming Lies of P sequel.As reported by FRVR, a filing on the European Union Intellectual Property Office indicates that Neowiz's new game will be titled Wonders of O. The first entry's title was a clear nod to its Adventures of Pinocchio themes, and so this new title seems to line up with previous reports that the sequel will be loosely based upon The Wonderful Wizard of Oz from author L. Frank Baum.Read the full article on nintendolife.com

item.title: Feature: Luigi's Mansion Is One Of My Favourite GameCube Games, But I've Never Actually Owned It

description.p: It just kept floating away.Today, 14th September 2026, marks the 25th anniversary of the Gamecube and, by extension, Luigi's Mansion. So to celebrate the occasion, Ollie looks back on Luigi's first spooky outing; a game he adored, but somehow never owned...I’ve always loved horror; it’s no secret at this point. So when Nintendo revealed Luigi’s Mansion as a GameCube launch title, I was all in from day one. It looked absolutely stunning: the spooky lighting, the creepy music, the swirling dust that kicks up when you walk around. Not only was it an excellent showcase for the follow up to the N64, but it just spoke to me on such a deep, visceral level.Read the full article on nintendolife.com

item.title: Hori Has Announced A Modular Arcade Stick For Switch 2, And It Looks Awesome

description.p: Have it your way.Accessory manufacturer Hori has announced a new, ambitious arcade stick for the Switch 2: the Hori Arcade Classic Pro.Officially licensed by Nintendo, the Classic Pro is unique in that it has two modular components on the left and right sides of the device. You've got four directional control options: a standard arcade stick, a trackball, a paddle, and a loop lever. The latter functions like an arcade stick, but you can also rotate the lever for an additional control scheme. So you can swap out the module as you see fit, making for quite a customisable experience.Read the full article on nintendolife.com

item.title: Nintendo Updates Zelda Timeline, Seemingly Confirming A Fan Theory

description.p: Links to the past.Nintendo has often stressed its desire to place gameplay above all else, including story. Yet with the company providing (and updating) an official Legend of Zelda timeline, fans have understandably become quite invested in the entire concept.Now, with the upcoming release of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Switch 2, Nintendo has once again updated the timeline, seemingly confirming a fan theory in the process. To explain as simply as we can (and with lots of help from Zeltik's video above), there is a theory that there are 'two' Hyrules: one founded following the events of Skyward Sword, and another after the timeline's reunification and prior to the events of Breath of the Wild.Read the full article on nintendolife.com

item.title: Feature: What I Learned After Working On Over 1,000 Switch 2 Joy-Con

description.p: The joys and cons.Coming into this console generation with the spectre of Switch 1's Joy-Con drift debacle in our minds, reviewers approached the Switch 2's Joy-Con with extreme caution. The controllers seemed much improved, but problems take time to manifest, and even when things do go wrong, knowing whether you've got a one-off dud or a widespread issue is difficult.With that in mind, we invited Gal Silver of GameTraderZero to share his thoughts, having disassembled and worked on hundreds of Joy-Con 2s in the 15 months since we first got our hands on them...Read the full article on nintendolife.com
